messages:
support: @ops ACME integration reporting streaming responses that drop ~2-3s into the stream. Client sees ECONNRESET and they were billed as 5xx. Customer pasted a small repro and a tokenized bill sample. Asking for triage and whether we should refund.

support: Repro curl they used:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8k","input":"stream test\n", "stream": true}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

ops: pulling gateway logs for r-req-id=r-ACME-9f2. can you paste the exact request id?

support: request id r-ACME-9f2. Customer timestamp: 2026-03-14T14:05:10Z. They included gateway log excerpt: 

support: ```
[2026-03-14T14:05:10.341Z] r-ACME-9f2 CLIENT -> gateway: new stream, chunked body start
[2026-03-14T14:05:12.912Z] gateway -> upstream: request forwarded to runtime node gpu-12
[2026-03-14T14:05:13.021Z] runtime gpu-12 -> gateway: first token chunks out
[2026-03-14T14:05:15.334Z] gateway: read error from client: ECONNRESET (fd 123)
[2026-03-14T14:05:15.335Z] gateway -> runtime: upstream connection closed unexpectedly (RST)
[2026-03-14T14:05:15.336Z] gateway: classified as 5xx, emitted 500 metric, billed tokens: 1.2k
```

devon: that sequence looks like client reset then gateway forwarded an RST to the runtime. We currently treat upstream RST that occurs before explicit trailer/frame as a server failure.

allen: is the client FIN coming before the runtime actually finished streaming? If the client half-closes immediately after receiving enough tokens, we should mark it as client-abort, not a 5xx.

marina: I reproduced with VS Code extension quickly: extension opens streaming conn, reads ~3s of tokens, then user stops the cell which triggers the client TCP FIN. On our side runtime sends small tail but the gateway receives the FIN and flips to RST and we count as 5xx.

ops: looks like an edge race between client FIN and our proxy flush handling. Two suggestions: (1) update EOF heuristic to prefer client-abort if we observed client FIN within 200ms of last client activity and we already emitted at least one chunk to client; (2) add an explicit late-trailer vs halfclose check in the gateway.

allen: agree. We should also emit a separate metric 'stream.client_abort' instead of incrementing 5xx so billing/pager rules don't trigger.

devon: low-risk hotfix: treat errors where gateway read error == ECONNRESET and runtime already sent >0 bytes as client-abort for billing only. Will open PR to metric mapping.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-112 created and linked to r-ACME-9f2.

support: Customer asked for refund for the 3 events in their invoice. Can we approve for now while dev works the fix?

ops: approve provisional credit for ACME for the three occurrences between 2026-03-14T14:04:30Z - 2026-03-14T14:06:00Z. I'll create a billing ticket and mark as pending root-cause.

customer-ops: customer wants timeline + mitigation note. Please include: explanation that we misclassified short client disconnects as server 5xx, and that we will patch heuristics and update billing.

marina: adding repro steps in GH issue: short interactive clients can trigger TCP FIN -> ECONNRESET race. Workaround: keepalive on client every 5s or let server finish stream.

devon: PR created  (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2147) with metric mapping + 200ms client-fin window. Running canary now on staging.

ops: staging canary shows zero new 5xx for the test case. Will promote to prod with 1-hour ramp.

support: forwarding timeline and refund confirmation to ACME. Thanks all :thumbsup:

allen: follow-up action: add an alert rule to compare stream 5xx vs stream.client_abort; if ratio spikes > 0.2 then page ops.

support: noted. closing loop with ACME after prod rollout.
